skills.name: orchestrate
skills.description: Run work of 3+ independently verifiable commits as an orchestrator: split into units, brief one builder per unit in its own worktree, land and commit each unit, gate once.
skills.whenToUse: Use for a task of three or more independently verifiable commits, or on request at any size.

skills.name: context-transfer
skills.description: Package this conversation into one self-contained block for a new chat: goal, decisions with reasons, verified progress, next steps.
skills.whenToUse: Use for a handoff, a context transfer, or a next-session prompt.

skills.name: human-voice-writing
skills.description: Draft or revise longer text the user sends or publishes as their own, so it reads human, not AI-generated.
skills.whenToUse: Use for messages, emails, posts and articles the user will send or publish under their name.

skills.name: memory-review
skills.description: Sort Claude Code's auto memory by the memory rule - preferences into rules, project knowledge into repo docs, progress deleted. Read-only until approved. Run with /memory-review.

skills.name: codebase-research
skills.description: Research code cheaply: skip agents when you know the file, pick researcher or general-purpose, always pass haiku or sonnet, cap reports at 30 lines.
skills.whenToUse: Use before spawning any agent to read or search code, or when a question needs several exploratory reads.

skills.name: release-notes
skills.description: Write or update a release note: entry format, required sections, the Fixed rule, and regenerating the release index.
skills.whenToUse: Use when asked to write or update a release note or changelog entry, and before reporting work on a release branch as done, so its open note covers every commit.

skills.name: feature-pr-description
skills.description: Write the body of a feature or fix PR from the branch's real diff, following the repo's PR contract.
skills.whenToUse: Use when asked to write, draft or update a PR description for a feature or fix branch. A release, promotion or hotfix PR goes to promotion-pr-description.

skills.name: promotion-pr-description
skills.description: Write a release or hotfix PR body (into staging or main) from its release note, plus what developers need before and after the merge.
skills.whenToUse: Use when asked to write, draft or update the description of a release, promotion or hotfix PR: a release branch into staging, staging into main, or a hotfix branch into either.

skills.name: thorough-diff-review
skills.description: Thorough local review of a diff: bugs, architecture boundaries, security, translations, conventions, reuse. Staged changes by default, or a branch, range or PR.
skills.whenToUse: Use before pushing, or when asked to review local changes, a branch or a PR.

skills.name: i18n-translate
skills.description: Translate added or changed source-locale message keys into every target locale, one haiku subagent per locale, then run the repo's translation check.
skills.whenToUse: Use before pushing a change that adds or edits user-facing strings.

skills.name: qa-tester
skills.description: QA a change in the running product on each surface it touched (web, API, CLI, native or mobile app, game, library): saved evidence, pass or fail per case, repro steps.
skills.whenToUse: Use after a change to prove it works in the running product, to reproduce a reported bug, or for a smoke pass.

skills.name: impact-check
skills.description: Check what a change could break outside its diff, name the premise it is safe because of, and prove that premise by running the real code.
skills.whenToUse: Use before merging a diff you don't fully trust, or for 'what could this break' and 'is this safe to merge'.

skills.name: how-it-works
skills.description: Explain how a part of the codebase works for the person about to change it: what it is, its moving parts, the flow with file:line refs and a diagram, where to start, traps.
skills.whenToUse: Use for 'how does X work', 'explain this subsystem or flow', or getting oriented in unfamiliar code before changing it.

skills.name: pr-review-triage
skills.description: Triage a PR: collect AI review findings, failed CI checks and open human threads, verify each at the PR head, and write a fix plan that proves every fix safe.
skills.whenToUse: Use when the message is a bare PR link, or when asked to triage a PR's review findings or failing checks.

skills.name: walkthrough
skills.description: Show what a finished change did and prove it works with its evidence: a short markdown note after any change, or a customer-facing HTML walkthrough of a release.
skills.whenToUse: Use when asked to walk through, recap or show what changed and the evidence it works ('walk me through the change', 'show me what changed', 'prove it works'), or for a customer release walkthrough.

skills.name: writeups-cleanup
skills.description: Propose what in a repo's writeups/ folder can go (merged and released changes, superseded releases, scratch) and delete only what the user approves. Run with /writeups-cleanup.

agents.name: builder
agents.description: Implements one unit of an orchestrated run in its own git worktree, gated but never committed; the orchestrator lands and commits it. Spawned by the orchestrate skill with a pointer to the unit's brief.

agents.name: qa
agents.description: QAs a finished change in the running product on every surface it touched, then writes the walkthrough; writes only evidence and notes into writeups/. Spawned by orchestrate after the gate.

agents.name: researcher
agents.description: Read-only code research for one factual question; reports at most 30 lines of paths, line ranges and facts. Spawned by codebase-research and by orchestrate's fact-gathering step.

agents.name: reviewer
agents.description: Read-only review of one orchestrated unit's worktree against its brief, with the thorough-diff-review checklist; reports at most 20 lines. Spawned by orchestrate for large units.
